changelog: Insert a new Core Principle prohibiting cuts inside numeric expressions to prevent splits of numbers, multipliers, units, percents or range endpoints (addresses the primary_finding: numeric splits like "340 million to 500 million" that harm cohesion, especially in short-latency bins).

Replace C7 to explicitly forbid cutting a verb (or auxiliary) from its core object/complement or from following prepositional/infinitival complements, because the primary finding shows verb+argument splits cause orphaned predicates and major cohesion loss.
Replace E1 with labeled example en_us_1116 to teach the scorer about harms from splitting numeric phrases and tiny trailing fragments (strong ≤3-bin loss).
Replace E2 with labeled example en_us_419 to show range/number+multiplier splits (e.g. "340 million to 500 million") that break cohesion in short-latency bins.
Replace E3 with labeled example en_us_1050 to surface breaks inside numeric measurements (meters, decimals) and unit splits that led to mistranslation.
Replace E4 with labeled example en_us_538 to highlight tiny trailing fragments and predicate/argument fragmentation that cause short-bin losses.

Insert a Core Principle that prescribes good cut placement for numeric expressions: keep numeral + multipliers + unit together, or if unavoidable cut before the whole phrase or after its unit — addresses the primary finding by describing a GOOD cut instead of a blanket ban.
